topic: ORM vs Raw SQL in Modern Full-Stack Development

post.topic: ORM vs Raw SQL in Modern Full-Stack Development
post.linkedin_text:
Be honest: Are ORMs saving you time or hiding your bugs?

Early in my journey, I used ORMs for everything. They feel like pure magic when you scaffold an MVP in a weekend.

Type safety out of the box, automatic migrations, and zero handwritten queries.

Then traffic spikes.

Suddenly, an innocent-looking nested query triggers an accidental N+1 problem behind the scenes, hammering your PostgreSQL database with 500 queries instead of one.

Here is how I look at it today:

• Heavy ORMs (like Prisma or TypeORM) shine for CRUD apps, admin panels, and rapid prototyping.
• Lightweight query builders (like Drizzle or Kysely) give you type safety without hiding the generated SQL.
• Raw SQL is still king for complex analytics, batch jobs, and performance bottlenecks.

Abstractions are great until they leak. If a developer cannot write the raw SQL query behind their ORM call, debugging production latency becomes a nightmare.

Where do you currently stand on your stack: Full ORM, lightweight query builder, or pure SQL?

slides.title: ORM vs *Raw SQL*: Where Do You Stand?
slides.body: The modern database debate every full-stack developer faces.

slides.title: The Promise of Modern ORMs
slides.body: ORMs offer fast prototyping, type safety, and automatic migrations. You can build entire CRUD APIs without touching a line of raw SQL.

slides.title: The Hidden Production Cost
slides.body: Abstractions leak under load. Lazy loading can cause silent N+1 queries, turning one simple API request into hundreds of database round-trips.

slides.title: The Rise of Query Builders
slides.body: Tools like Drizzle and Kysely bridge the gap: you write SQL-like structures with TypeScript safety, keeping full visibility over execution.

slides.title: When Raw SQL Still Wins
slides.body: Complex aggregations, window functions, and bulk data operations almost always run cleaner and faster as pure, optimized SQL queries.

slides.title: Which Side Are You On?
slides.body: Do you prefer high developer velocity with ORMs, or the transparency and performance of SQL? Drop your stack in the comments.
